blocks.text: Hum parh chuke hain ke current le jane wale conductor ke gird magnetic field paida hoti hai (Fig. 10.1). Isi tarah badalti magnetic field us mein rakhe conductor mein current paida karti hai. Electromagnetism physics ka aham shoba hai jo parhta hai ke electric charges aur magnetic fields aapas mein kaise taamul (interact) karte hain.

blocks.title: Oersted, 1820
blocks.text: 1820 mein Hans Christian Oersted (print mein 'Orsted') ne maloom kiya ke bijli aur magnetism aapas mein jure hain: taar mein current qareeb rakhi compass ki sui ko hila deta hai, kyunke current apne gird magnetic field banata hai.

Electromagnetism jadeed technology, jaise phones, computers aur tibbi aalaat, ke liye lazmi hai. Is chapter mein hum electric fields, magnetic forces aur electromagnetic induction jaise bunyadi tasawwurat parhenge, aur dekhenge ke yeh usool qudrati mazahir aur technology dono par kaise asar karte hain. In tasawwurat ki samajh se pata chalta hai ke electromagnetism hamari duniya par kaise asar karta aur nayi ijadat ko aage barhata hai.

Magnetism ki shuruat lodestone se hui, jo qadeem Turkiye mein daryaft hone wala qudrati maadni maadda (mineral) hai. Lodestone, ya magnetite (Fe3O4), loha aur steel jaisi dhaaton ko khainch sakta hai aur Zameen ke magnetic poles ke saath seedh mein aa jata hai, jis se compass ijad hua (For Your Information).

blocks.prompt: Bijli ki line mein current shimal (north) ki taraf beh raha hai. Taar ke bilkul oopar magnetic field ki simt kya hai (MCQ 10.1)?
blocks.explanation: Right-hand grip rule se, angootha current ke saath shimal ki taraf rakhne par ungliyan is tarah murti hain ke taar ke bilkul oopar maghrib (west) ki taraf ishara karti hain. Jawab (d) west hai.

items: Current magnetic field banata hai, aur badalti magnetic field current banati hai; electromagnetism charges aur magnetic fields ka taamul parhta hai. Oersted (1820) ne bijli aur magnetism ka rishta dikhaya.
Qadeem Turkiye ka lodestone (magnetite, Fe3O4) loha aur steel khainchta hai aur compass ki bunyad bana.
